Between us touching the ceiling, passing halfway through the season, or after the All-Star game, I really wanted to do this segment. But now it seems like a good opportunity to do it before we slip into the playoffs. There are still three games left in the season and playoff games. So, for now, let's not touch the ceiling yet. But from my perspective, in the first place, Minnesota is a surprise team that has done an incredible job. Everyone talked about last year's terrible trade by Gobert and how the second unit didn't live up to expectations. They made mistakes and delayed their future, but now they're blocking those high-flying guards like Edwards, and everyone spoke at the beginning of the season about trading KAT for Towns, but they're currently in second place in the league with what seems like the best defense, and Rudy Gobert reminds us why he was Defensive Player of the Year so many times. **Speaker 00** Moving on to other teams. Behind them is a team that's a bit surprising, Oklahoma City. Like Indiana, it's a young team without experience, but more dangerous and more skilled. No one expected them to be in second place, let alone in the Western Conference. And, of course, we can't forget about Lou Dortch, who's a defensive stopper, Josh Giddey, with incredible game vision, and Jalen Williams, who also gave us a great season. **Speaker 00** And then there's another team in the West that will surprise you - Dallas Mavericks. They had Luka and Donte Exum, and maybe we'll see them again in the playoffs against Jannis or Embiid, and that's what you need - someone who can give them the spark, the energy, the body under the basket. **Speaker 00** So, yes, there are some great teams out there.
